_about: OUR position tags for candidates on specific issues, each sourced to the candidate's own words or recorded votes as reported. Levels describe a position, never a character judgment (see docs/data-model.md, "Stances"). A candidate with no entry has no sourced position: show nothing, never a guess. `text` is a one-line factual summary; quotes are the candidate's.

topics.label: Police surveillance tech
topics.description: License plate readers (Flock, Axon, Motorola and others), police drones and camera networks.

levels.vendor: Against Flock, open to another vendor

topics.label: Police staffing & budget
topics.description: Whether to grow the police force and its budget, hold the budget where it is, or move work to non-police responses.

topics.label: Police union support
topics.description: Endorsements and direct contributions from police, deputy sheriff and other peace-officer unions.

Stephen Sherrill.text: Answered “yes” on increasing surveillance tech, crediting license plate readers for a drop in car break-ins; says the facial-recognition ban must stay. Backs Flock so far, but would oppose it “if civil liberties are impacted.”
Answered yes to “try to achieve full staffing for SFPD” (about 2,100 officers; SFPD counted 1,565 in Nov 2025), and wants to keep “staffing SFPD and expanding safety technology.”

Matt Dorsey.text: Supports renewing SF’s Flock contract and expanding plate readers and drones; open to guardrails against misuse, but opposes limits “premised on speculative harms.”
Wants SFPD to “commit to a three-year plan to reach 100% full staffing, full stop”; wrote two charter amendments on police staffing.

Emanuel “Manny” Yekutiel.text: “Yes, I support it, with real guardrails”; won’t support any of it “if that data ends up with ICE or the federal government, full stop.” Has “no allegiance to Flock.”
Answered yes to “try to achieve full staffing for SFPD” (about 2,100 officers; SFPD counted 1,565 in Nov 2025): “We’ll make it safer by fully staffing our police department.”

Darshini Patel.text: Would vote against renewing SFPD’s Flock contract: “a violation of our personal privacy.”
Agrees running SFPD on overtime “costs more than staffing it properly,” but says “none of that requires a bigger budget.”

Michael T. Nguyen.text: Opposes expanding Flock cameras: “a mass-surveillance system that tracks where people travel.”

Gary McCoy.text: Doesn’t support the city’s use of Flock cameras; says he has refused donations from Flock, its lobbyists and employees.

Theo Ellington.text: Supports renewal only with strict retention limits, independent audits, public reports and “an absolute bar” on sharing data with immigration enforcement.

Answered yes to “try to achieve full staffing for SFPD” (about 2,100 officers; SFPD counted 1,565 in Nov 2025); wants assigned foot patrols on commercial corridors alongside violence-prevention funding.

J.R. Eppler.text: Would vote no on expanding surveillance in D10. Calls plate readers and drones useful tools, but “Flock failed the test”: SF should pick a new vendor after a Police Commission review.
Answered yes to “try to achieve full staffing for SFPD” (about 2,100 officers; SFPD counted 1,565 in Nov 2025).

Dionjay (DJ) Brookter.text: Would oppose expanding “Flock and other mass-surveillance technology”: “We should not create systems that track residents’ movements.”

Shawn M. Richard.text: Answered yes to “try to achieve full staffing for SFPD” (about 2,100 officers; SFPD counted 1,565 in Nov 2025); stresses retention, de-escalation training and health-first responses to drug and mental-health calls.

Mike Trouble Lin.text: Answered yes to “try to achieve full staffing for SFPD” (about 2,100 officers; SFPD counted 1,565 in Nov 2025); “a vocal supporter of fully funding SFPD including foot patrol units.”
Would back “more flock cameras and drones.”

Charlene Wang.text: Voted for Oakland’s Flock contract (Dec 2025) and wrote its safeguards; now says “I have concerns with Flock” and is “actively pushing the city for an open bid to replace Flock.”
Says “OPD is severely understaffed”; serves on the mayor’s OPD recruiting task force and is building cadet and community recruiting programs.

Nate Adams.text: “I do not support the City contracting with Flock and oppose renewal”: opposes “this use of mass surveillance.”
“We can’t solve national trends by simply pouring money into recruitment”; wants alternatives like MACRO so OPD can focus on calls that need an armed response.

Janani Ramachandran.text: Voted for Oakland’s two-year Flock contract (Dec 2025, 7–1, with only Carroll Fife against).

Kevin E. Jenkins.text: Voted for Oakland’s two-year Flock contract (Dec 2025, 7–1, with only Carroll Fife against).

Nancy S. Sidebotham.text: “OPD needs to increase its staffing of officers to 1000 or more.”

Daria Wrubel.text: Opposes plate readers and would end the Flock contract; pledged never to vote to “approve, renew, expand, or otherwise allow any mass surveillance system.”

Moni Gangopadhyay.text: Opposes plate readers (“These cameras don’t prevent crime”) and would end the Flock contract; signed the same no-mass-surveillance pledge.

Laura Babitt.text: Would end the Flock contract (“a bad actor”); skeptical of more surveillance spending, open to cameras against illegal dumping. Didn’t say whether she opposes plate readers in general.

Ross Bernet.text: Prefers a plate-reader vendor other than Flock (would consider Flock only with adequate data controls); wouldn’t approve the police drone and camera expansion package.

Steve Kromer.text: Would “probably” vote against Flock; open to another vendor, and would convene police and the Police Accountability Board to find a “balance point.”

Igor A. Tregub.text: Voted against renewing Berkeley’s Flock plate-reader contract (May 2026, passed 5–4); the council rejected the drone and camera expansion 8–1.

Majdi \"Gaith\" Abuhamdieh.text: Joined an Oct 6 press conference denouncing mass surveillance technology, including plate-reader cameras.

Aidan Hill.text: Joined an Oct 6 press conference denouncing mass surveillance technology, including plate-reader cameras.

Syrak Micael.text: Joined an Oct 6 press conference denouncing mass surveillance technology, including plate-reader cameras.

Mark Humbert.text: Voted to renew Berkeley’s Flock contract in May; calls the readers “really useful in solving some really serious crimes,” while sharing concern about federal access.

Michael Wallman.text: Opposes plate readers and police surveillance tech: “I’m just against mass surveillance.” Doesn’t think Berkeley can safeguard the data.

Mari Mendonca.text: Wants Berkeley to end the Flock contract and calls plate readers “an unsafe option”: “Surveillance is not a strategy; it’s surveillance.”

Claudia Jiménez.text: Voted against turning Flock’s plate readers back on (Mar 2026, passed 4–3). Richmondside reports she first voted for a Flock contract and now wants an assessment of its effectiveness and data sharing with immigration enforcement.

Police already get about 35% of the city budget and budgeted positions go unfilled; says even a 1% increase would cut other services, and would invest in youth jobs, crisis response (ROCK), parks and cleanup.

Ahmad Anderson.text: Backed the Flock cameras earlier in the campaign; now ties them to minimum police staffing and wants civil-liberties rules with consequences for misuse.
Has the support of Richmond’s police association, per KQED.
Wants more police money, technology and officers; backs the police union’s proposed 187-officer minimum (143 are budgeted). Reimagining safety “doesn’t mean defunding, doesn’t mean reallocating.”

Chris Sturken.text: Cast the only no vote on Redwood City’s first Flock contract (Sept 2023, 6–1), citing weak privacy protections and the risk of misreads.

Alan Wong.text: Answered yes to “try to achieve full staffing for SFPD” (about 2,100 officers; SFPD counted 1,565 in Nov 2025); would back “a budget that adequately supports” SFPD and civilianize desk jobs to move officers to patrol.

Barbara Lee.text: Any Flock renewal needs an independent review verifying limits on data access, sharing and retention, a ban on immigration-enforcement or protest monitoring, and public reporting.
Wants to recruit and keep more officers: restored the Cadet Program, and would improve supervision and wellness and “shift appropriate administrative work to civilian staff.”

Brenda F. Grisham.text: “I will support flock cameras 100% as I have in the past and would push for renewing the system.”
Blames attrition on “a slow hiring process”; would speed up police and dispatcher recruitment.

Mindy Ruth Pechenuk.text: “The Flock cameras have been a great tool to our police.”
“The problem is NOT the OPD”; says Oakland must match other cities’ officer pay and equipment.

Julius Robinson.text: Would renew Flock “only if an independent review demonstrates public-safety value,” with privacy protections.
“I would pursue a credible plan toward the 700-officer benchmark,” with “competitive compensation within our fiscal capacity.”
